about: Data for /storm/charles/. Every line is taken from the weather desk's sourced facts (desks/weather-vicky/live.md, s41-lead.json, as of its 21:37 UTC check) and Web Summit's public statement; nothing is added. Refresh from live.md each time the desk changes it; reviewer@ verifies before publication. Times are UTC = Lisbon time in November.

lead.headline: Web Summit: Day 2, Wednesday 11 November, will not take place
lead.text: On the Portuguese Government's formal advice, Web Summit has said Day 2 will not take place. It says it aims to proceed with Day 3, Thursday 12 November, as planned, following the passing of Storm Charles.
lead.source_label: Web Summit's statement "Important event update" (dated 19:09 UTC in its page data; on its blog by about 20:00 UTC), read 23:45 UTC. Web Summit also emailed attendees, and its homepage carries the notice.
lead.source_note: The government's formal advice itself has not been found on an official page.

alerts.what: Wind: ORANGE, Wed 11 Nov 09:00 to 21:00. Gusts up to 120 km/h. IPMA lowered it from red (12:00 to 21:00, gusts up to 120 km/h, possibly 140 km/h in the most exposed places) in its update of 08:15 UTC on Wednesday.
Rain: RED, Wed 11 Nov 09:00 to 18:00. Heavy and persistent rain. Orange from 07:17 to 09:00. IPMA moved the start of the red warning earlier from 12:00 to 09:00 on Tuesday evening.
Sea: ORANGE, Wed 12:00 to 21:00, south-west waves of 5 to 7 m, up to 13 m maximum; then yellow until Thu 03:00. Re-read at 08:41 UTC: unchanged.

Alert situation (situação de alerta) for all of mainland Portugal, 00:00 to 23:59 on Wednesday: schools and non-essential public services closed; outdoor events suspended, whatever their nature; no access to parks and wooded areas at risk of falling trees; no access to the shoreline, rivers and flood-prone areas.
Asked people to stay at home where possible and avoid unnecessary travel. An appeal, not an order.
Raised the special readiness state and sent a public SMS warning about Wednesday.

alerts.who: Maritime Authority and the Navy (the weather desk's read; not re-checked)
alerts.what: Considerable worsening of the weather and the sea on the mainland from 06:00 on Wednesday to midday on Thursday. This is their forecast for the sea and the coast, not IPMA's land warning for Lisbon; the two figures are not the same.

summit.status: Web Summit says Day 2, Wednesday 11 November, will not take place, respecting the Government's direction, and that it aims to proceed with Day 3, Thursday 12 November, as planned, following the passing of Storm Charles. Its homepage says: "On the advice of the Portuguese Government, Day 2 of Web Summit will not be going ahead due to severe weather warnings."
open: What Day 3 will look like beyond "aims to proceed as planned": not announced.
The government's formal advice to Web Summit, on any official page: not found by the desk.
Any measure of the City of Lisbon (its sites refuse automated reads): not read.

from_authorities.text: The government's measures apply on Wednesday: outdoor events are suspended, parks and wooded areas at risk of falling trees and the shoreline are off limits.
The Minister of Internal Administration appealed to people to stay at home where possible and avoid unnecessary travel.

Web Summit's statement gives the reasons for cancelling Day 2 as the risks from Storm Charles, including tidal flooding, severe disruption to public transport and the impact of high winds on external structures.

transport.name: Fertagus (trains over the 25 de Abril bridge)
transport.text: Trains running normally at 08:00 UTC, its notice says. The notice still says that if winds exceed 90 km/h, trains on the bridge will be suspended, possibly on the whole line; it recommends avoiding non-essential travel. (Read 09:05 UTC.)

transport.name: Carris (city buses and trams)
transport.text: Its homepage banner says service is disrupted, that Carris is monitoring the situation and will post changes, and to check before leaving. First read at 18:37 UTC; still there at 23:43. No suspension named.

transport.name: Carris Metropolitana (regional buses)
transport.text: Four general weather notices run to Wednesday 23:59: possible disruption, delays and diversions. Seven lines (4404, 4405, 4406, 4412, 4414, 4415, 4422) run shortened routes from 04:00 to 11:00 on Wednesday because of the weather. No suspension announced.

transport.name: Transtejo/Soflusa (river ferries)
transport.text: Wednesday: the Porto Brandão–Trafaria–Algés ferry link is interrupted, because the authorities have closed the Algés seafront promenade; passengers use the Trafaria–Porto Brandão–Belém link (notice of 22:28 UTC on Tuesday). Tuesday's 13:24 suspension of car transport was lifted at 18:06.

transport.name: Metro de Lisboa
transport.text: No change to Metro service found on Metro's site. Metro keeps five stations open on the nights of 10 to 11 and 11 to 12 November to shelter homeless people, with the Lisbon and Amadora councils.

transport.name: CP (national rail) and the airport (ANA)
transport.text: Not readable by our tools; not checked. Check them directly.

not_announced: Any suspension of Metro, Carris or Carris Metropolitana for Wednesday, or a closure of the Tagus bar.
The City of Lisbon's own measures (its sites refuse automated reads).
The government's formal advice to Web Summit, on any official page.

timeline.text: IPMA lowers Lisbon's wind warning for Wednesday from red to orange (09:00 to 21:00, gusts up to 120 km/h); the red rain warning (09:00 to 18:00) stays. IPMA's data was modified at 08:15 UTC; we read it at 08:41 UTC.
IPMA moves the start of Lisbon's red rain warning for Wednesday to 09:00 (orange from 00:00 to 09:00); the red wind warning (12:00 to 21:00) is unchanged. (Seen by about 23:41 UTC.)
Transtejo/Soflusa publishes the Wednesday notice: the Porto Brandão–Trafaria–Algés ferry link is interrupted because the authorities closed the Algés seafront.

Web Summit's statement "Important event update" is on its blog (dated 19:09 in its page data): the Government has formally advised that Day 2 should not take place, because of Storm Charles (tidal flooding, severe disruption to public transport, wind on external structures). Its homepage carries the notice.
Metro de Lisboa keeps five stations open overnight on 10 to 11 and 11 to 12 November for homeless people, citing the forecast worsening of the weather.
Carris's homepage banner reads that service is disrupted and that it is monitoring the situation.
IPMA raises Lisbon's rain warning to red for Wednesday 12:00 to 18:00 (later moved to start at 09:00); the red wind warning is unchanged.
PRESS: the Prime Minister says the government recommended suspending the summit's work; the decision was the organisers' (24 Notícias).
IPMA communiqué no. 2 on the depression CHARLES: worse weather from early Wednesday morning; red and orange warnings issued; track and strength highly uncertain.
PRESS: the Lisbon mayor says everything indicates Web Summit cannot run on Wednesday; the decision is for the Ministry of Internal Administration (DN).
Transtejo/Soflusa suspends car transport on Trafaria to Porto Brandão to Belém for rough seas; service is restored at 18:06 UTC.
The Maritime Authority and the Navy warn of a considerable worsening at sea from Wednesday 06:00 to Thursday midday. (The weather desk's read; not re-checked.)
The government declares the alert situation for all of mainland Portugal on Wednesday (the page's date).
ANEPC's Aviso 21 on CHARLES: gusts to 120 km/h; avoid unnecessary travel. (The weather desk's read; not re-checked.)
IPMA communiqué no. 1 names the low CHARLES and says orange warnings will follow, an upgrade not ruled out.
